title: Operator Surface Authority Spec
description: Input shape for scripts/surface_authority_audit.mjs — a normalized description of which operator surface (Scout, FleetBar, pd-console) owns each capability, its distance-from-work classification, evidence weight, daemon-enforceability, and hot/cool bus subscription.

capabilities.description: Every capability the three operator surfaces expose, one entry per (capability, surface) claim. A capability legitimately claimed by two surfaces will appear twice with different assignedSurface values — that duplication is exactly what the auditor is built to catch.

assignedSurface.description: Which of the three operator surfaces renders this capability.

distance.description: Distance-from-work classification: intake (Scout, inside the artifact), ambient (FleetBar, glanceable consent), deep (pd-console, seated full-evidence inspection).

evidenceScreens.description: Number of distinct screens/panes of evidence a human needs to evaluate this capability's state before acting on it.

daemonEnforceable.description: True only if the daemon can actually back/enforce the control being rendered (acceptance criterion 6: controls are enabled only when the daemon can actually enforce them).

busSubscription.description: Which message plane this capability subscribes to: hot (ephemeral, in-process multiplexed WebSocket: presence, current step, stream cursors, steering) or cool (append-only, replayable: Work Intents, plans, claims, transcript events, gate decisions, receipts).

surfacesOwnRuntimeState.description: True if any surface owns runtime state directly instead of rendering daemon truth. Must be false: 'no surface owns runtime state; all three render daemon truth and submit commands through the same envelopes.'
